Summary Statistics

Source: R/stats.R
stats_summary.Rd

Calculates descriptive statistics for environmental monitoring data.

Usage

stats_summary(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
stats_summary(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  censored = "censored",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  default_unit = "default_unit",
  result_col = analysis_result,
  censored_col = censored,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
stats_summary(
  df,
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  censored_col = censored_var(df),
  na.rm = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'grouped_df'
stats_summary(df, ...)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location_id

Location column name.

param_name

Analyte column name.

censored

Censoring indicator column name.

analysis_result

Analytical result column name.

default_unit

Reporting unit column name.

result_col

Numerical column on which stats_summary is computed.

censored_col

Censoring indicator column name used to calculate detection counts and censoring percentages.

na.rm

Logical indicating whether missing values should be removed when calculating summary statistics.

Value

A tibble containing one row per summary group.

The returned table includes:

n

Number of records in the group, including records with missing result values.

n_used

Number of non-missing analytical results used in statistical evaluations and decision selection.

n_detect

Number of non-censored analytical results.

percent_censored

Percentage of records in the group classified as censored.

mean

Arithmetic mean concentration.

median

Median concentration.

sd

Sample standard deviation.

var

Sample variance.

min

Minimum concentration.

max

Maximum concentration.

cv

Coefficient of variation.

25%

25th percentile.

75%

75th percentile.

IQR

Interquartile range.

mad

Median absolute deviation.

censoring_class

EPA Unified Guidance style censoring classification: low_censoring, moderate_censoring, high_censoring, or extreme_censoring.

distribution_method

Recommended distributional approach based on the degree of censoring.

trend_method

Recommended trend method.

trend_guidance

Recommended interpretation of trend results. "formal_trend_test" indicates trend inference is generally supported. "screening_only" indicates trend results should be considered exploratory because of extensive censoring.

censored_method

Recommended censored-data handling method for trend analyses.

decision_basis

Basis for the statistical recommendation. Examples include: fewer_than_4_observations, low_censoring, moderate_censoring, high_censoring, and extreme_censoring.

Details

For `env_schema` objects, calculations are performed using the standardized `.analysis_result` and `.censored` columns rather than the original source data columns. This ensures summary statistics are based on the processed analytical values used throughout the package.

If the input is grouped with [dplyr::group_by()], summary statistics are calculated within the existing groups. For ungrouped inputs, summaries are calculated separately for each location, analyte, and unit.

For ungrouped `data.frame` inputs, summaries are calculated by:

  • location

  • analyte

  • reporting unit

For ungrouped `env_schema` inputs, summaries are calculated by:

  • the mapped location variable returned by `location_var()`

  • the mapped analyte variable returned by `analyte_var()`

  • the standardized analysis unit (`.analysis_unit`)

Missing result values are excluded from statistical calculations when `na.rm = TRUE`, but still contribute to the record count (`n`), which represents the number of records in each summary group.

Empty inputs return an empty tibble with the standard summary columns.

env_schema Method

For `env_schema` objects, `stats_summary()` automatically uses the schema mappings and standardized analytical fields:

  • `.analysis_result`

  • `.censored`

  • `.analysis_unit`

This allows summaries to remain consistent regardless of the original source column names or schema mappings used by the input data.
